title: Automating API Workflows With Playwright
excerpt: Automating API workflows with Playwright makes it possible to catch backend issues long before they ever reach the UI.
html:
API testing is often associated with Postman, and for good reason. It remains one of the most effective tools for exploring endpoints, validating responses, and understanding how APIs behave.

As test coverage grows, however, automation becomes increasingly important.

One thing that stood out while automating APIs with Playwright is how efficiently complex API workflows can be automated and maintained as a project scales. Instead of manually repeating requests and managing data between steps, entire flows can be executed programmatically, making tests more repeatable and easier to integrate into CI/CD pipelines.

A well-designed API test should go beyond a "200 OK" response and validate:

  • Response structure and data types
  • Dynamic values such as tokens and generated IDs
  • Business logic and expected outcomes
  • End-to-end API workflows such as Create → Get → Update → Get → Delete → Get

A particularly useful aspect of Playwright is having API and UI testing within the same framework. Test data can be created through an API, validated through additional API calls, and then verified in the UI when needed, all within a single test suite.

Perhaps one of the most interesting takeaways is how many issues can be uncovered without touching the UI at all. Testing APIs directly provides visibility into how the backend handles authentication, business logic, data, and service interactions.

Catching problems at that stage often makes them easier to diagnose and resolve before they ever become visible to end users.
